title: The Hollow of the Ninefold Court
premise: Wren Sterling has survived nine years as the crown's food-taster by being forgettable—except he is also the quiet keeper of ledgers for the Ninefold Court, a guild that trades in impossible things: borrowed years, bottled grief, souls pawned against bad harvests. When a purge of the gifted begins, Wren learns his own name sits in the oldest ledger, sold to the court beneath the mountain before he could walk. To survive, he must steal back his own soul before the moon completes its thirteenth turn, aided by Ilse Vane, the inquisitor hunting him who cannot bring herself to name him guilty. In the hollow beneath the mountain, Wren discovers the guild's founder is his own mother, still alive and holding his soul as collateral for a debt the crown itself incurred; he wins it back not by theft but by paying the true price—his immunity, his safety, and his place at court—and returns to the surface to testify, choosing truth over the invisibility that once kept him alive.
about_author: Theo Quintana is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing debt records from vanished merchant houses, an experience that left a permanent fascination with what people will trade away. They write fantasy about small people inside large machinery, and live somewhere with too many stairs.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Wren. A routine morning tasting for the Lord Chancellor turns lethal when Wren detects nightshade laced into a honeyed pear—but swallowing it anyway to protect his cover as merely skilled, not gifted. Introduces his double life: taster by day, ledger-keeper for the Ninefold Court by night. Emotional beat: the exhaustion of performing ordinariness.

chapters.title: Ledgers of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Wren. In the guild's cellar office, Wren records the week's trades—a widow selling her grief, a soldier buying back three lost years—and notices an entry flagged with the royal seal: a soul held 'beneath,' payment date due at the thirteenth moon. He doesn't yet know whose soul it is. Emotional beat: complicity dressed up as bookkeeping.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The crown announces a hunt for the gifted; registration or pyre. Wren watches neighbors line up to denounce each other and realizes his immunity regimen has made him the perfect suspect—only the immune survive accidental poisonings so calmly. First appearance of Inquisitor Ilse Vane, watching him across the square. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Ilse Vane
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. The inquisitor interviews Wren formally and finds nothing—too neatly nothing. She keeps his file on her desk instead of filing it, telling herself she's being thorough. Flashback to why she joined the hunt: a gifted sister burned years ago while Ilse stood silent. Emotional beat: duty beginning to chafe.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon
chapters.summary: POV Wren. An almanac confirms the thirteenth moon falls in forty days. The guild's master, Corvess, warns Wren that when the flagged entry comes due, the court beneath the mountain collects in person. Wren finally reads the full entry and finds his own name, entered the day of his birth. Emotional beat: vertigo—the past was always hunting him.

chapters.title: What the Crown Owes
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Digging through sealed archives, Wren learns the truth: decades ago the crown bought a famine's end from the Ninefold Court and pledged a royal-blooded soul as surety. His mother, a hidden princess, traded his soul to save the realm—and then vanished. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid by someone else, on your behalf.

chapters.title: A Debt in Ash
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Investigating a poisoning at court, Ilse traces the nightshade to someone protecting Wren—or framing him. She confronts him privately off the record, and he lies badly. Instead of arresting him, she burns the page of testimony, an act that terrifies her more than treason would. Emotional beat: love against duty, first crack in the wall.

chapters.title: The Guild Turns
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Corvess offers Wren a way out: surrender another soul in his place—the guild's books must balance. Wren refuses, and Corvess marks him as a liability, selling his location to the inquisition. The guild that sheltered him becomes the trap. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth—the institution was never loyal to him.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Salt Market
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Inquisitors raid the cellar office; Wren escapes through the salt market with only the oldest ledger under his coat, wounded by a hexed net that burns the gifted. Ilse arrives moments late and knows, looking at the blood, exactly who escaped. Emotional beat: running as a way of life ending.

chapters.title: The Road Beneath
chapters.summary: POV alternating Wren/Ilse. Ilse catches Wren at a mountain shrine—and instead of taking him in, asks him the one question no one else asked: what was taken from you? He tells her everything. She chooses, provisionally, to walk with him as far as the mountain's mouth. Emotional beat: two enemies becoming allies over shared complicity.

chapters.title: The Hollow Gate
chapters.summary: POV Wren. They descend through the salt market's drowned twin into the court beneath the mountain, where debts are lit by candlelight and every transaction echoes forever. Wren presents himself to pay his own ransom and is told the debt isn't his to settle—it belongs to whoever holds his soul. Emotional beat: hope curdling into bureaucratic horror.

chapters.title: The Founder
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Led deeper, Wren meets the guild's founder: his mother, alive, sustained by the court because her death would void the crown's contract and collapse the trade. She has kept his soul safe all these years—not stolen, guarded. But guarding it means she can never leave, and never be known. Emotional beat: love against duty, embodied.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. The court offers terms: Wren may reclaim his soul if someone of equal weight takes his place in the ledger. Ilse quietly begins negotiating to substitute herself, hiding it from Wren. Meanwhile word reaches them that the purge above has escalated—Corvess has testified that the inquisitor herself is gifted. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered in secret.

chapters.title: Thirteen Candles
chapters.summary: POV Wren. With days left before the thirteenth moon, Wren studies the original contract and finds the flaw: the crown pledged a soul, not a person—and a pledge made by a regent without royal assent is voidable. But voiding it requires testimony from both parties before the court, meaning his mother must confess her identity publicly. Emotional beat: the legalism of miracles.

chapters.title: What Corvess Sold
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Above ground, Ilse's former colleagues arrive to arrest her; she talks her way free long enough to send warning down the mountain. Interlude revealing Corvess's motive: he founded nothing—he usurped the founder's seat and needs her dead and the contract intact. Emotional beat: betrayal wearing the mask of order.

chapters.title: The Court Assembles
chapters.summary: POV Wren. On the eve of the thirteenth moon, the Ninefold Court convenes to collect. Wren stands before nine masked magistrates and invokes the flaw in the contract. Corvess, arriving with inquisitorial escort, produces forged documents claiming the founder is dead. The court demands proof of life. Emotional beat: the whole book's tension compressed into one hearing.

chapters.title: My Mother's Name
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren's proof is not a document but a confession: he names his mother before the court, knowing that doing so makes her mortal again and himself a target of every power that profited from her erasure. She steps forward, aged and luminous, and confirms it. The forged papers burn. Emotional beat: truth as the only currency that clears the debt.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The court rules the contract void—but balance demands payment. Wren surrenders his immunity, the gift he built dish by dish, pouring it back into the ledger. He leaves the hollow ordinary, poisonable, human. His mother, freed, chooses to stay one night to teach him the one thing she can: how to live unhidden. Emotional beat: grief and release entwined.

chapters.title: Ascension
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Climbing out of the mountain, they find the purge collapsing—without the guild's secret enforcement, the hunt loses its teeth. Ilse submits her own resignation and her own confession to her superiors, accepting whatever follows. She and Wren part at the gate without promises, which is its own kind of promise. Emotional beat: duty rewritten rather than abandoned.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren returns to the capital and does the unthinkable: testifies openly before the Chancellor about the crown's old debt and the purge's true engine, using the ledger as evidence. He expects the pyre; instead, scandal forces the regime to bury the hunt quietly. He is dismissed from service—free, unemployed, and visible for the first time. Emotional beat: survival redefined as living in the open.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Months later, Wren opens a modest counting-house that helps people exit impossible contracts honestly—no souls, no pawns. His mother visits as a stranger sometimes; Ilse sends letters with no return address. The last entry in his new ledger is his own name, written freely, owned by no one. Emotional beat: peace earned, not inherited.

chapters.title: Coda: What the Moon Counted
chapters.summary: POV brief, omniscient-leaning Wren. On the night the thirteenth moon completes, Wren tastes a meal cooked by his own hand—untested, unfeared—and raises a cup toward the mountain. Somewhere below, a candle goes out that had burned for thirty years. Short, quiet chapter closing the arc of the moon motif. Emotional beat: gratitude without forgetting the cost.
